purpose: Approved conversation notebook and source viewer component target.
prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: ONE high-fidelity component mockup of the After Class conversation notebook and source viewer, in their actual desktop app context.
Direction name: The Conversation Desk.
Create realistic, production-quality UI designs with clear hierarchy, strong typography, intentional imagery, and purposeful spacing.

THIS IS AN APPROVAL MOCKUP, not implementation. User wants exactly one component mockup, then will sign off before an implementation handoff is written. Preserve their approved visual direction and core tutoring experience; do not explore unrelated new styles or mascots.
Target dimensions: 1440 x 1024 desktop web-app frame, full viewport. One coherent screen, no multiple alternatives, no component inventory board, no device/browser chrome. Current date anchor November 3 2026 America/Los_Angeles; omit visible dates.

INPUT IMAGES:
Image 1: prior After Class Last Desk scene. This is the PRIMARY composition, material and brand reference: warm paper, tactile honey wood, mint chalkboard, sharp navy geometric shadows, finely inked isometric objects. Reuse that world, but reduce decorative scene footprint so this is practical for sustained tutoring.
Image 2: prior Projection Booth scene. Secondary reference only for SOURCE VIEWER: legible lecture frame, timestamp, plain link; do not adopt its dark full-room background.
Image 3: Mote original mascot study. Character identity reference: cream book moth, amber antennae, dusty-blue crescent on folded page-shaped wings, blue waistcoat and small ochre satchel. Keep Mote SMALL and quiet in this actual lesson view.
These are reference images for generating a new screen, not edit targets. No new mascot designs.

PRODUCT STATE: Active Socratic review, after learner has made a first attempt and explicitly opened a citation. The CURRENT MAIN QUESTION and one answer plus current follow-up are visible together. No answer-giving recap before attempt. Tutor and learner text are clearly distinct. The source is captured evidence, not live YouTube playback. No fake video player controls that suggest unsupported embedded video playback. No mastery/XP/score/streak/progress percentages, no decorative metrics or achievements, no premature saved-success claim. No complex graph or library inventory.

SCENE AND LAYOUT:
Very light ivory paper base, subtle fine texture behind art only; dark ink, dusty cobalt primary accent, muted mint and honey wood. Crisp hand-inked solids with precise four-tone shading, refined dimensional edges, soft small real shadows, not glossy clay or photorealistic CGI.
Header around 68px: small yellow bell + "After Class" at left; at right small "My notebook", "Pause", and discreet "End review". No giant marketing headline. Under header compact title "Locks & deadlocks" (30px serif), small subtitle "Reviewing 00:00–12:40 · 1 lecture". Main body starts around y160.
Left 36% is the source stand, right 64% is the conversation notebook. Comfortable margins 40–48px and a clean 28px gutter. A slim honey-wood desk edge and a little mint chalkboard corner frame the left lower/background area, enough to evoke the approved Last Desk scene. Do not fill half the screen with decorative furniture. The ACTUAL interface text is always front-facing, never tilted into isometric perspective.

LEFT SOURCE VIEWER:
Hinged dimensional lecture stand inspired by the PRIMARY reference, with mustard frame, tiny side brackets, metal feet, restrained real depth. Paper evidence sits on it facing front for legibility. Header "Lecture evidence", smaller "Opened by you", accessible close icon top right.
A clear original purpose-made captured lecture slide, title "Circular wait", readable diagram: two boxes "Thread 1" / "Thread 2"; inside "holds A" / "holds B"; blue arrows between boxes labeled "waits for B" / "waits for A". Diagram has accurate circular wait relations and roomy labels, not lots of tiny text. Under frame simple caption "Captured frame · 06:42", then a fine rule and "YouTube captions · 06:42–07:03". Short transcript quotation verbatim: "Each thread holds a lock while waiting for the other." Small link "Open in YouTube ↗". No timeline/playback bar, no invented live-video integration. A quiet footnote link "Review scope & coverage" stays secondary.
Source viewer occupies roughly y190–770, not boxed twice; real material frame contains source paper.
Mote sits at the bottom-left foot of the stand, around 70–85px tall, relaxed folded wings, no speech bubble, gaze toward the notebook. Beside it a small cobalt physical recorder around 95x55px has a subtle mic symbol and a plain engraved label "Speak"; it mirrors the visible Speak control. Scene art must support readability and never cover text.

RIGHT CONVERSATION NOTEBOOK:
An open cream notebook page with a single thin red margin line and small binder-ring perforations down its left edge, subtle dimensional page edge, no nested colored chat cards. Main readable conversation area around 760px wide, body 17–18px / 1.5 line height, question/follow-up 24–26px, comfortable line lengths. At top small "QUESTION 1 OF 3" and quiet "Earlier in this question" label over history. Preserve clear attributions "AFTER CLASS" and "YOU" using typography and tiny colored margin marks, not giant avatars.

Exact chronological dialogue:
AFTER CLASS
"Two threads are waiting on each other. How could that happen?"
YOU
"One holds lock A and wants B. The other holds B and wants A."
Separate history from current follow-up with ONE fine horizontal rule, a little whitespace, and small label "FOLLOW-UP".
AFTER CLASS
"What would have to change for either thread to continue?"
Beneath the follow-up a small selected citation link "Lecture · 06:42" with a tiny open-source icon, visually tied to the opened stand at left. No extra source explanation that answers this follow-up.

ANCHOR THE COMPOSER at the bottom of the notebook, independent of scrolling conversation above; subtle scroll affordance on history's right edge. Composer is a generous flat lightly ruled answer area around 150px tall, label "Your response", placeholder "Think it through, in your own words…". No text draft required, clear caret indicates ordinary keyboard input. Below a restrained microphone icon button "Speak", strong cobalt main button "Share my thinking", and small "Ctrl Enter". On the last quiet row "A little hint" and "More options" (for explain, skip, don't know, dispute). No wall of every possible action. State here is READY FOR LEARNER, not currently recording, tutor speaking or thinking; do not show conflicting state indicators.
Do not show autosaved/saved banners while the review is still in progress. No fake correctness judgments.

TYPOGRAPHY AND DENSITY:
Two fonts maximum: warm literary serif for After Class and dialogue headings; readable humanist sans-serif for body and controls. Body 17–18px, labels 12–13px, avoid tiny decorative mono type everywhere. Dark warm ink text, strong readable controls, restrained blue accents. Use spacing, grouping, alignment and dividers before surface tints, borders only where functional, minimal shadows except the physical stand/page. Keep all controls inside viewport. Calm, adult-playful, specific and beautiful. This must look like a practical next stage of the approved isometric classroom desk, not a generic dashboard, flashcard, or large illustration next to an empty textbox.
approval: User: yeah that looks fine, please write an implementation doc for the three scenes and the mascots.
